newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close down, Kia troubles depress.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close down, Kia troubles depress.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly lower on Saturday as sentiment continued to be depressed by the uncertain future of the troubled Kia Group, brokers said.
Friday's meeting of Kia's creditor banks failed to reach agreement on detailing their earlier decision to bail out the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate.
The composite index closed 1.02 points lower at 730.43.
"Trading was slow as sentiment continued to be volatile amid uncertainty about Kia's problems," said Kim Ik-hwan, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
Brokers said investors were worried over the delayed settlement of Kia's troubles that surfaced in mid-July when creditor banks selected the group for bail-out.
But Kisan rose 380 won to its limit of 5,200 won on news that Hyundai Engineering and Construction agreed to buy about 80 billion won worth of land from Kisan.

Jinro General Foods, a unit of another troubled conglomerate, the Jinro Group, also went limit-up to 3,710 won, by gaining 270 won after its creditor Hanil Bank said it would offer a five billion won emergency loan.
